questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hari Parbat Fort in Srinagar was originally built during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: The Hari Parbat Fort's outer wall (known as 'Koh-i-Maran') was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1590. Jahangir is associated with the Shalimar Bagh garden. Shah Jahan is linked to Chashme Shahi garden. Aurangzeb had limited construction activity in Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dogra dynasty of J&K:

(i) Maharaja Gulab Singh became the first Dogra ruler through the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846.
(ii) Maharaja Ranbir Singh succeeded Gulab Singh and promoted Sanskrit learning.
(iii) Maharaja Pratap Singh's reign saw the establishment of the Praja Sabha.
(iv) The Dogra rule ended with the signing of the Simla Agreement in 1972.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Gulab Singh acquired J&K through the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. Statement (ii) is correct — Ranbir Singh (ruled 1857-85) was a patron of Sanskrit and established libraries. Statement (iii) is correct — Pratap Singh (1885-1925) introduced the Praja Sabha in 1922. Statement (iv) is incorrect — Dogra rule ended with the Instrument of Accession in 1947, not the 1972 Simla Agreement.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Martand Sun Temple near Anantnag is one of the most important archaeological sites of Kashmir.
Reason (R): It was built during the Karkota dynasty (8th century CE) and represents the finest example of Kashmiri temple architecture.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Martand is a major archaeological/historical site. Reason (R) is correct — it was built by Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty (725-756 CE) and showcases the zenith of Kashmiri stone architecture. Its architectural significance (R) directly explains why it is important (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical places in J&K with their associated rulers/builders:

Column I:
(a) Shalimar Bagh
(b) Nishat Bagh
(c) Chashme Shahi
(d) Pari Mahal

Column II:
(i) Prince Dara Shikoh
(ii) Asaf Khan
(iii) Shah Jahan
(iv) Emperor Jahangir

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh was built by Emperor Jahangir in 1619 (a-iv). Nishat Bagh was created by Asaf Khan, brother of Nur Jahan (b-ii). Chashme Shahi was built during Shah Jahan's reign in 1632 (c-iii). Pari Mahal was built by Prince Dara Shikoh as a school of astrology (d-i). Option B swaps Shalimar with Nishat. Option C mismatches Nishat with Shah Jahan. Option D incorrectly places Shalimar with Shah Jahan.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly associated with Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah) of Kashmir?

(i) He promoted religious tolerance and cultural harmony.
(ii) He encouraged art, literature, and craftsmanship.
(iii) He introduced paper-making, shawl-weaving, and carpet-making to Kashmir.
(iv) He built the Jama Masjid of Srinagar.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah, 1420-1470) was known for religious tolerance (i correct), patronage of arts and literature (ii correct), and introducing crafts like papier-mâché, shawl-weaving, and carpet-making from Central Asia (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the Jama Masjid was originally built by Sultan Sikandar (1389-1413), Budshah's father, not by Budshah himself.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Burzahom archaeological site in Kashmir is famous for:
options: Neolithic and Megalithic period remains including pit dwellings
Buddhist monastery ruins from the Kushan period
Medieval fortifications of the Sultan dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: Neolithic and Megalithic period remains including pit dwellings
questions.explanation: Burzahom (near Srinagar) is a significant prehistoric site containing Neolithic (c. 3000 BCE) pit dwellings, stone tools, and megalithic structures. It is NOT a Mughal site (gardens are in other locations). It is not a Buddhist monastery (that would be Harwan). It is not a medieval fort but a prehistoric settlement site.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Shankaracharya Temple:

(i) It is situated on Gopadri (Takht-i-Sulaiman) hill in Srinagar.
(ii) The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
(iii) It is believed to date back to around 200 BCE (Mauryan period).
(iv) It was built by the Mughal Emperor Akbar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Shankaracharya Temple sits on Takht-i-Sulaiman/Gopadri hill (i correct). It is dedicated to Lord Shiva (ii correct). It dates to approximately 200 BCE based on architectural analysis (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the temple predates the Mughals by over a millennium; Akbar built the Hari Parbat Fort wall, not this temple.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Treaty of Amritsar (1846) was signed between:
options: British East India Company and Maharaja Gulab Singh
Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the British
Maharaja Hari Singh and the Indian Union
questions.correctAnswer: British East India Company and Maharaja Gulab Singh
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846) was between the British East India Company and Maharaja Gulab Singh, transferring the territory of J&K to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. Ranjit Singh died in 1839. Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession in 1947. 'Dogra Confederacy' is not a recognized entity in this context.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Lohara dynasty is considered the longest-ruling dynasty of Kashmir.
Reason (R): The Lohara dynasty ruled Kashmir for approximately 250 years from 1003 CE to 1320 CE.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Lohara dynasty had the longest rule in Kashmir's history. Reason (R) is correct — they ruled from approximately 1003 to 1320 CE (about 317 years in two branches). The duration mentioned in (R) directly supports and explains why they are considered the longest-ruling (A). Option B is wrong because the duration is the very reason. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mubarak Mandi Palace complex in Jammu was the royal residence of:
questions.explanation: Mubarak Mandi Palace in Jammu served as the official residence of the Dogra rulers of J&K from the 19th century. It was not a Mughal governor's residence (they stayed in Kashmir). Sikh rulers (Ranjit Singh's empire) had their base in Lahore. Afghan rulers had no connection to this palace.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Afghan rule in Kashmir (1753-1819):

(i) It is characterized by oppression, heavy taxation, and decline of arts.
(ii) Ahmad Shah Abdali's commander annexed Kashmir from the Mughals.
(iii) The Afghan period lasted for approximately 67 years.
(iv) The Afghans promoted Kashmiri Shaivism and Hindu culture.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Afghan rule (1753-1819) was marked by tyranny and heavy taxes (i correct). Kashmir was taken from the weakened Mughal governors by Ahmad Shah Abdali's forces (ii correct). The period lasted about 67 years until the Sikh conquest (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — Afghans did NOT promote Kashmiri Shaivism; their rule was generally oppressive toward non-Muslim traditions.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical sites with their locations in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Akhnoor Fort
(b) Avantipur Ruins
(c) Harwan Archaeological Site
(d) Bahu Fort

Column II:
(i) On the banks of River Tawi, Jammu
(ii) Near Srinagar (Kushan-period Buddhist site)
(iii) On the banks of River Chenab
(iv) Near Awantipora, Pulwama

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Akhnoor Fort is on the banks of the Chenab River (a-iii). Avantipur Ruins are near Awantipora in Pulwama district, built by King Avantivarman (b-iv). Harwan is a Kushan-period archaeological site near Srinagar with Buddhist terracotta tiles (c-ii). Bahu Fort is on the banks of the Tawi River in Jammu (d-i). Option B swaps Akhnoor with Avantipur. Option C mismatches Avantipur with Harwan. Option D incorrectly places Akhnoor on the Tawi.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Rajatarangini, the famous historical chronicle of Kashmir, was written by:
questions.explanation: Rajatarangini ('River of Kings') was written by Kalhana in 1148-1150 CE. It is the earliest known chronicle of Kashmir's history. Bilhana was a Kashmiri poet who moved to the Deccan. Jonaraja wrote a continuation of Rajatarangini covering later periods. Srivara continued Jonaraja's work. Only Kalhana is the original author.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired?

(i) Avantivarman — Founded Avantipur and built Hindu temples
(ii) Lalitaditya Muktapida — Built Martand Sun Temple
(iii) Shah Mir — Founded the first Muslim dynasty of Kashmir
(iv) Rinchana — Last Hindu ruler of Kashmir

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Avantivarman (855-883 CE) founded Avantipur and built temples there (i correct). Lalitaditya built the Martand Sun Temple in the 8th century (ii correct). Shah Mir established the first Muslim dynasty in 1339 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — Rinchana was NOT the last Hindu ruler; he was a Ladakhi Buddhist prince who converted to Islam. The last Hindu ruler was Kota Rani (queen of the Lohara dynasty).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sikh rule over Kashmir (1819-1846) began when:
options: Ranjit Singh's army under Misr Diwan Chand conquered Kashmir from the Afghans
The British handed Kashmir to the Sikhs
The Dogras gifted Kashmir to the Sikh Empire
Kashmir voluntarily joined the Sikh Confederacy
questions.correctAnswer: Ranjit Singh's army under Misr Diwan Chand conquered Kashmir from the Afghans
questions.explanation: In 1819, Maharaja Ranjit Singh's army, led by commander Misr Diwan Chand, defeated the Afghan governor and annexed Kashmir. The British didn't hand it over — they took it from the Sikhs later (1846). The Dogras didn't gift it — they acquired it FROM the British. Kashmir didn't voluntarily join — it was conquered militarily.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Jama Masjid of Srinagar is one of the most important historical mosques of Kashmir.
Reason (R): Originally built by Sultan Sikandar in the early 15th century, it has been destroyed and rebuilt several times and can accommodate over 33,000 worshippers.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Jama Masjid is one of Kashmir's most significant historical mosques. Reason (R) is correct — Sultan Sikandar built it in 1394 CE, it has been rebuilt after fires, and has a massive capacity. Its historical antiquity, resilience, and scale (R) explain its importance (A). Option B is wrong because (R) provides the direct reasons for its importance. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Pandrethan Temple:

(i) It is a small stone temple situated near Srinagar.
(ii) It was built during the reign of the Utpala dynasty (10th century CE).
(iii) It is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
(iv) It stands in the middle of a small spring-fed pool.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Pandrethan Temple is a small but architecturally significant stone temple near Srinagar (i correct). It was built during the Utpala dynasty period, around 10th century CE (ii correct). It is situated in the middle of a spring-fed tank/pool (iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — the temple is dedicated to Lord SHIVA (a Shiva lingam), not Vishnu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Shah Hamadan Mosque (Khanqah-e-Moula) in Srinagar is named after:
options: Mir Sayyid Ali Hamdani, a Persian Sufi saint
questions.correctAnswer: Mir Sayyid Ali Hamdani, a Persian Sufi saint
questions.explanation: Khanqah-e-Moula is named after Mir Sayyid Ali Hamdani (Shah-e-Hamadan), a 14th century Persian Sufi scholar who visited Kashmir and had a profound influence on Islamic culture there. Sultan Sikandar was a later ruler. Shah Jahan was a Mughal emperor with no connection to this mosque. Sheikh Noor-ud-din was a Kashmiri Rishi saint, not associated with this particular mosque.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The ancient fort of Hari Parbat is also known as 'Koh-i-__________' meaning 'Hill of Snakes' in local tradition.
questions.explanation: Hari Parbat is called 'Koh-i-Maran' (Hill of Serpents/Snakes) from the local legend about snakes inhabiting the hill. 'Koh-i-Sulaiman' is associated with the Shankaracharya temple hill (Takht-i-Sulaiman). 'Koh-i-Noor' is a famous diamond. 'Koh-i-Hasan' is fabricated.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following sultans/rulers of Kashmir with their contributions:

Column I:
(a) Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin
(b) Sultan Sikandar
(c) Queen Didda
(d) Lalitaditya Muktapida

Column II:
(i) First woman ruler of Kashmir, Lohara dynasty
(ii) Built the Jama Masjid and destroyed temples
(iii) Patron of arts, introduced paper-making and shawl-weaving
(iv) Expanded kingdom from Afghanistan to Bengal, built Martand

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah) was a patron of arts who introduced crafts (a-iii). Sultan Sikandar (Butshikan) built the Jama Masjid and destroyed many Hindu temples (b-ii). Queen Didda was the first woman ruler from the Lohara dynasty (c-i). Lalitaditya expanded the Karkota empire vastly and built Martand (d-iv). Option B swaps Zain-ul-Abidin with Sikandar. Option C mismatches Sikandar with Lalitaditya. Option D incorrectly pairs Zain-ul-Abidin with Didda.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Raghunath Temple in Jammu is one of the largest temple complexes in North India. It was initiated by:
options: Maharaja Gulab Singh and completed by Maharaja Ranbir Singh
Emperor Akbar during his Kashmir visit
Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin as a gesture of tolerance
questions.correctAnswer: Maharaja Gulab Singh and completed by Maharaja Ranbir Singh
questions.explanation: The Raghunath Temple was initiated by Maharaja Gulab Singh (first Dogra ruler) in 1835 and completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh. Emperor Akbar did not build Hindu temples in Jammu. Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin operated in Kashmir, not Jammu city. Ranjit Singh's Sikh empire did not build this temple.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chak dynasty of Kashmir:

(i) The Chak dynasty ruled Kashmir from 1561 to 1586 CE.
(ii) The Chaks were Shia Muslims.
(iii) Yusuf Shah Chak was the last ruler before Mughal conquest.
(iv) The dynasty was established after overthrowing the Mughals.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Chak dynasty ruled from approximately 1561 to 1586 (i correct). They were Shia Muslims (ii correct). Yusuf Shah Chak was the last Chak ruler, defeated by Mughal forces under Akbar in 1586 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the Chaks came to power by overthrowing the SHAH MIR (Sultanate) dynasty, not the Mughals. The Mughals actually ended Chak rule.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Amar Mahal Palace Museum in Jammu was built in which architectural style?
questions.explanation: The Amar Mahal Palace was built in the French chateau (castle) style with red sandstone, featuring sloping roofs and European design elements. It was built by a French architect for Maharaja Amar Singh. Mughal style features arches and gardens (different). Gothic style has pointed arches (found in churches). Rajasthani Haveli style is distinct from this European design.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Kashmir was conquered by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1586 CE.
Reason (R): The last Chak ruler, Yusuf Shah Chak, was defeated and Kashmir became part of the Mughal Empire for over 160 years.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Akbar's generals conquered Kashmir in 1586. Reason (R) is correct — Yusuf Shah Chak was defeated and Kashmir remained under Mughal rule until 1753 (about 167 years). The defeat of the Chak ruler (R) was the means by which (A) was accomplished, and the duration confirms Mughal consolidation. Option B is wrong because (R) explains how the conquest happened. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following historical places are located in the Kashmir Valley?

(i) Avantipur Temple ruins
(ii) Martand Sun Temple
(iii) Akhnoor Fort
(iv) Pandrethan Temple

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Avantipur ruins are in Pulwama district, Kashmir Valley (i correct). Martand Sun Temple is in Anantnag district, Kashmir Valley (ii correct). Pandrethan Temple is near Srinagar, Kashmir Valley (iv correct). Akhnoor Fort (iii) is located in the JAMMU region on the banks of the Chenab River, NOT in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mughal rule in Kashmir is generally characterized by:
options: Construction of gardens, relative peace, and cultural flourishing
Complete destruction of all local traditions
Introduction of Buddhism to the region
questions.correctAnswer: Construction of gardens, relative peace, and cultural flourishing
questions.explanation: The Mughal period (1586-1753) in Kashmir saw the creation of famous gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi), relative political stability, and cultural patronage. 'Complete destruction of traditions' is an exaggeration — Mughals were generally more tolerant. 'Introduction of Buddhism' is incorrect — Buddhism declined centuries earlier. 'Industrialization' is anachronistic for the Mughal era.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Instrument of Accession of J&K:

(i) It was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 October 1947.
(ii) It was accepted by Lord Mountbatten on 27 October 1947.
(iii) It covered the subjects of Defence, External Affairs, and Communications.
(iv) It was signed after the tribal invasion from Pakistan-administered areas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct. Maharaja Hari Singh signed on 26 October 1947 (i). Mountbatten accepted it on 27 October (ii). The accession covered Defence, External Affairs, and Communications (iii). The tribal invasion on 22 October 1947 prompted the Maharaja to seek Indian military help and sign the accession (iv).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hemis Monastery in Ladakh belongs to which Buddhist sect?
questions.explanation: Hemis Monastery, the largest and wealthiest in Ladakh, belongs to the Drukpa lineage of the Kagyu school (often called Red Hat sect). Gelug (Yellow Hat) is the Dalai Lama's school — associated with other monasteries. Theravada is practiced in Southeast Asia, not Ladakh. Zen is East Asian Buddhism, not Tibetan.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following periods of Kashmir's history with their rulers:

Column I:
(a) Hindu Period (855-1339 CE) — last major dynasty
(b) First Muslim Dynasty (1339-1561 CE)
(c) Sikh Period (1819-1846 CE)
(d) Dogra Period (1846-1947 CE)

Column II:
(i) Maharaja Gulab Singh to Hari Singh
(ii) Governors appointed by Ranjit Singh
(iii) Shah Mir Dynasty
(iv) Lohara Dynasty

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The last major Hindu dynasty before Muslim rule was the Lohara Dynasty (a-iv). The first Muslim dynasty was Shah Mir's (b-iii). During Sikh period, Kashmir was governed by appointed governors under Ranjit Singh (c-ii). The Dogra period saw rulers from Gulab Singh to Hari Singh (d-i). Option B swaps Lohara with Shah Mir. Option C mismatches Shah Mir with Sikh governors. Option D incorrectly places Dogra rulers with Hindu period.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Bahu Fort in Jammu is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Bahu Fort, one of the oldest structures in Jammu, stands on a rock face on the left bank of the River Tawi. The Chenab flows further north through Doda/Kishtwar. The Jhelum flows through the Kashmir Valley. The Ravi flows through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab, not Jammu city.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Rishi order of Sufism in Kashmir:

(i) Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (Nund Rishi) is considered the founder of the Rishi order.
(ii) The Rishi order blended Islamic mysticism with local Kashmiri spiritual traditions.
(iii) The order emphasized vegetarianism, renunciation, and living in harmony with nature.
(iv) It was introduced by Arab traders in the 7th century.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Noor-ud-din (Nund Rishi, 1378-1438) founded the indigenous Rishi order (i correct). The order uniquely blended Islamic Sufism with pre-existing Kashmiri Shaiva traditions (ii correct). Rishis advocated vegetarianism, asceticism, and nature harmony (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — the Rishi order developed in the 14th-15th century in Kashmir, not in the 7th century through Arab traders.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Harwan archaeological site near Srinagar contains terracotta tiles with Buddhist imagery.
Reason (R): During the Kushan period (1st-3rd century CE), Buddhism flourished in Kashmir and various monasteries and stupas were built.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Harwan has significant terracotta tiles with Buddhist motifs. Reason (R) is correct — the Kushan period saw Buddhism prosper in Kashmir (King Kanishka hosted the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir). The Buddhist flourishing during the Kushan era (R) explains why Harwan has Buddhist artifacts (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains the historical context. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Fourth Buddhist Council' was held in Kashmir during the reign of which king?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Buddhist Council was held in Kashmir (at Kundalvana/Harwan) during the reign of Kushan Emperor Kanishka in the 1st-2nd century CE. Ashoka convened the Third Council at Pataliputra. Lalitaditya ruled in the 8th century, long after the council. Avantivarman ruled in the 9th century.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are historical forts located in the Jammu region?

(i) Bahu Fort
(ii) Akhnoor Fort
(iii) Hari Parbat Fort
(iv) Bhimgarh Fort (Reasi)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Bahu Fort is in Jammu city on the Tawi river (i correct). Akhnoor Fort is in Jammu division on the Chenab (ii correct). Bhimgarh Fort is in Reasi district, Jammu division (iv correct). Hari Parbat Fort (iii) is in SRINAGAR in the Kashmir Valley, not in the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Karkota dynasty's most famous ruler, Lalitaditya Muktapida, is known for:
options: Expanding the kingdom from Central Asia to Bengal and building the Martand Sun Temple
Signing the Treaty of Amritsar with the British
questions.correctAnswer: Expanding the kingdom from Central Asia to Bengal and building the Martand Sun Temple
questions.explanation: Lalitaditya (725-756 CE) created a vast empire stretching from Central Asia to Bengal and built the magnificent Martand Sun Temple. He did not introduce Islam — that happened centuries later. The Treaty of Amritsar was 1846. Rajatarangini was written by Kalhana in 1148 CE.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dal Gate area in Srinagar:

(i) It marks the main entrance to the Dal Lake.
(ii) The British Residency was located nearby during Dogra rule.
(iii) Mughal gardens line the eastern bank in this area.
(iv) It has been a commercial and cultural centre since ancient times.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Dal Gate is the main entrance/point to Dal Lake (i correct). The British Residency (now a hotel) was indeed located in this area during the Dogra era (ii correct). It has been a commercial hub for centuries (iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — Mughal gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi) are on the EASTERN shore/foothills of the Zabarwan range along the lake, not specifically at Dal Gate itself which is at the southwestern end.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The historical chronicle 'Rajatarangini' written by Kalhana in __________ CE is the most important source for the ancient and medieval history of Kashmir.
questions.explanation: Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini in approximately 1148-1150 CE (some sources say 1148). 1050 is too early. 1250 is after Kalhana's time (continuations were written then). 900 is significantly before Kalhana's era.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following Mughal gardens with their unique features:

Column I:
(a) Shalimar Bagh
(b) Nishat Bagh
(c) Chashme Shahi
(d) Achabal Garden

Column II:
(i) Known as 'Royal Spring' with the smallest of Mughal gardens
(ii) 'Abode of Love' with four terraces
(iii) 'Garden of Joy' with twelve terraces
(iv) Known for its natural spring source in Anantnag

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh means 'Abode of Love' and has four terraces (a-ii). Nishat Bagh means 'Garden of Joy' and has twelve terraces (b-iii). Chashme Shahi means 'Royal Spring' and is the smallest Mughal garden (c-i). Achabal Garden in Anantnag is famous for its natural spring source (d-iv). Option B swaps Shalimar with Nishat. Option C mismatches Nishat with Chashme Shahi. Option D incorrectly pairs Shalimar with Achabal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the approximate ruling periods of different dynasties in Kashmir:

| Dynasty | Period | Duration (years) |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| Karkota | 625-855 CE | 230 |
| Utpala | 855-939 CE | 84 |
| Lohara | 1003-1320 CE | 317 |
| Shah Mir | 1339-1561 CE | 222 |

Which dynasty ruled for the longest period?
questions.explanation: The Lohara dynasty ruled for approximately 317 years, the longest among the listed dynasties. Karkota ruled for 230 years (second longest). Shah Mir ruled for 222 years. Utpala ruled for only 84 years (shortest). The data clearly shows Lohara at 317 years.

The following data shows the number of historical monuments in different districts of J&K (approximate):

| District | Temples | Mosques/Shrines | Forts | Total |
|----------|---------|-----------------|-------|-------|
| Srinagar | 8 | 15 | 2 | 25 |
| Anantnag | 12 | 6 | 1 | 19 |
| Jammu | 10 | 5 | 3 | 18 |
| Pulwama | 5 | 4 | 0 | 9 |

Which district has the highest proportion of temples to its total historical monuments?
questions.explanation: Anantnag: 12/19 = 63.2%. Jammu: 10/18 = 55.6%. Srinagar: 8/25 = 32%. Pulwama: 5/9 = 55.6%. Anantnag has the highest proportion of temples (63.2%) among its total monuments, due to sites like Martand Sun Temple and other ancient Hindu ruins.
